# UPPAbaby Mesa V3 (US)

- **Id:** `uppababy-mesa-v3`
- **Category:** car-seat
- **Status:** shortlisted
- **Price:** $349.99
- **Brand:** UPPAbaby
- **Maker's page:** <https://uppababy.com/car-seats/infant/mesa-v3/james/>
- **Decision:** none yet

## Summary

Fits the same UPPAbaby strollers as the Aria V2, with a 32 in height limit and three ways to install without the base. Its base has no load leg, and BabyGearLab found its LATCH install not the most stable in the group. The carrier weighs about 10.9 lb (measured). NHTSA rated the older V2 5 stars for ease of use; the V3 is not rated.

## Safety

- **Standards:** FMVSS 213, FMVSS 213a
- **FMVSS 213a (decision 0001):** recorded
- **Recall search last run:** 2026-11-27
- **Recalls:** none found in the search of 2026-11-27

## Pros

- Baseless European-routing install "remarkably stable compared to competitors", no towel (BabyGearLab V3).
- Three baseless methods allowed (European, optional lap/shoulder, lap-only), so it has a fallback in taxis (V3 manual).
- 32 in height limit, longer than the Aria V2 and KeyFit 30 (manual).
- NHTSA ease-of-use rated the Mesa V2 5 stars in every category; V3 not rated (older version).
- Canopy "one of the best in the group" and never hits the handle (BabyGearLab V3).
- No-rethread harness with 25 headrest positions (maker).

## Cons

Misuse risks come first.

- **Misuse risk:** a CPST saw the base's tightness indicator show green while the base was "still way too loose" (The Car Seat Lady, original Mesa base; same base family, not retested on V3). Always do the manual's 1-inch movement test.
- **Misuse risk:** two owners report the base indicator going from green back to red while driving (Babylist, 2026-09-29), the same symptom Aria V2 owners report. Low confidence.
- **Misuse risk:** the lock-off does little to hold the base on a vehicle belt; it "rocked fairly easily" under force (BabyGearLab V3). LATCH install avoids this.
- Several owners report a newborn's head falling chin to chest; one baby failed a car seat test with the newborn insert and passed without it (Babylist owner reviews). Low confidence.
- Consumer Reports has not tested V3; the Mesa V2 scored 68 (24th of 46) and is not CR Recommended (read through Nick's CR account).
- Carrier measured 10.9 lb on V3, against the maker's 9.9 lb (BabyGearLab).
- Buckle is stiff to press; the latch plates must be pulled out (BabyGearLab V3).
- Manual mixes a "bubble" instruction with its green/red level marker (V2 and V3 manuals).
- Stroller range is UPPAbaby strollers plus Mockingbird adapters; not on Thule's chart (market survey).
